neet_che_u12_t00_1.working: In Werner's theory, primary valency is ionisable and equals the oxidation state. It is satisfied by anions. Secondary valency is non-ionisable, equals the coordination number and fixes the geometry.

neet_che_u12_t00_2.working: 0.02 mol AgCl from 0.01 mol complex means 2 ionisable Cl- per formula unit. For Co(III) with coordination number 6 this gives [CoCl(NH3)5]Cl2.

neet_che_u12_t00_3.working: Count ions per formula unit: [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] gives 0, [CoCl(NH3)5]Cl2 gives 3, [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 gives 4, K4[Fe(CN)6] gives 5. Molar conductivity rises in that order.

neet_che_u12_t00_4.working: [CoCl2(NH3)4]Cl has only one counter Cl-, so it gives 1 mol AgCl, not 3. A is false. R is true because only ions outside the coordination sphere are precipitated.

neet_che_u12_t00_5.working: Co(III) has primary valency 3 and coordination number 6, so I is correct. The compound ionises to [CoCl(NH3)5]2+ + 2Cl-, which is 3 ions and a 1:2 electrolyte, so II is incorrect.
